title: Four Great Lakes showed no clear change in ice maximum rank correlation between 1973-1999 and 2000-2026
abstract: We tested whether annual maximum ice cover became more closely linked across Superior, Michigan, Huron and Erie. We used a fixed NOAA GLERL table for 54 winters. The mean of six Spearman rank correlations rose from 0.823 in 1973-1999 to 0.906 in 2000-2026. The change was +0.083, with a conditional 95% three-winter block interval of -0.048 to +0.321. All planned check intervals included zero. Winters with at least three lakes below fixed early-period 25th-percentile cutoffs rose from 7 to 12. The count stayed at 7 under period-specific cutoffs. Thus more joint low-ice winters alone do not establish stronger dependence. The diagnostic is not a causal decomposition or a tail dependence test. Short records, climate persistence, changing charts, bounded cover and revised data limit inference. The package includes code, aggregate results, bootstrap draws, provenance, a figure and arithmetic checks. Source records remain external.

display.caption: Six lake-pair rank correlations and late-minus-early mean changes. All conditional 95% block intervals include zero. S, M, H and E mean Superior, Michigan, Huron and Erie.
